AtT‐ 20 cells express the isozymes α, ∝, β, γ and ζ, that these isozymes are differentially involved in the secretory process, that the α, ∝ and ζ isozymes are involved in the regulation of the calcium signal and the β isozyme is involved in the control of calcium entry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of hormone secretion from endocrine cells.
the role of PKC isozyme(s) in the regulation of ACTH secretion.
the role of PKC in modulating ACTH secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the α isozyme of the PKC acts distal to calcium and at the GTP‐binding proteins to modulate the calcium‐evoked secretion of ACTH and that the β isozyme acts proximal to calcium to modulate the cytosolic concentration of calcium.

PKC isozyme activation can act at two sites in the secretogogic pathway for ACTH release, the first site being at the level of a GTP‐dependent protein and the second site being at the plasma membrane.
the PKC is a multifunctional enzyme that acts at multiple sites in the secretogranin‐dependent pathway of ACTH secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the β isozyme acts to regulate calcium influx and that the α and ∍ PKC isozyme act to modulate the effects of calcium on the secretory pathway.
PKC isozyme activation can enhance the ability of increased calcium concentrations and GTP‐binding proteins to stimulate ACTH release.
the β isozyme acts at a site proximal to the calcium‐evoked secretory pathway to modulate the cytosolic concentration of calcium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PKC‐α isozyme is the most important PKC isozyme for the regulation of ACTH secretion in AtT‐ 20 cells.
PKC isozyme subtypes have differential effects on ACTH secretion and these effects may be exerted at different stages in the ACTH secretion pathway.
